title: The Bremen Town Musicians
note: A new shortened adaptation of the Brothers Grimm tale as printed in Dinah Maria Mulock Craik’s public-domain collection.

rights.basis: Source edition published in the nineteenth century and identified as public domain by Project Gutenberg.

artLabel: A donkey, dog, cat, and rooster make music beneath a cottage window.
scenes: An old donkey left home and set out for Bremen. “Perhaps I can become a town musician,” he thought.
On the road he met an old dog, an old cat, and a rooster in trouble. “Come with me,” said the donkey. “Together we can make music.”
At night they saw a cottage where robbers feasted. The animals stacked themselves—donkey, dog, cat, then rooster—and performed their loudest song through the window.
The terrified robbers fled. When one crept back, the cat scratched, the dog barked, the donkey kicked, and the rooster crowed from the roof. He raced away with a wild tale of monsters.
The four friends found the cottage so comfortable that they never reached Bremen.
They had set out to become musicians, and in their own noisy fashion, music had found them a home.
